The differential equation that generates the slope field shown above is given by ${y}^{′}=(y-a)(y-b)^{2}.$ Find the value of $ab.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040443/assets/68f424470a3a8ff98d7f738ce207c240795185e48ee527a434d04282d9023ed7.png)

Notice that the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $y=1$ and $y=4,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines.

So, our differential equation must be

$$
{y}^{′}=(y-1)(y-4)^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $a=1,b=4,$ and $ab=4.$
